diabetes.answer:
**Diabetes** is a chronic metabolic disease characterized by elevated blood sugar levels. There are two main types:

• **Type 1**: The body doesn't produce insulin (autoimmune)
• **Type 2**: The body doesn't use insulin properly (lifestyle-related)

**Common Symptoms**: Excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision

**Prevention**: Regular exercise, balanced diet, maintain healthy weight, regular checkups

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Endocrinologist**

hypertension.answer:
**Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)** is when blood pressure against artery walls is consistently too high.

• **Normal BP**: Below 120/80 mmHg
• **Elevated**: 120-129/<80 mmHg
• **High (Stage 1)**: 130-139/80-89 mmHg
• **High (Stage 2)**: 140+/90+ mmHg

**Risk Factors**: Obesity, high salt intake, stress, lack of exercise, family history

**Prevention**: Low-sodium diet, regular exercise, limit alcohol, manage stress

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Cardiologist**

malaria.answer:
**Malaria** is a life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through infected mosquito bites.

**Common Symptoms**: High fever, chills, headache, nausea, muscle pain, sweating

**Prevention**: Use mosquito nets, insect repellent, wear long sleeves, eliminate standing water

**Treatment**: Anti-malarial medications (prescribed by doctor)

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **General Physician / Infectious Disease Specialist**

dengue.answer:
**Dengue Fever** is a mosquito-borne viral infection common in tropical regions.

**Common Symptoms**: High fever, severe headache, pain behind eyes, joint/muscle pain, rash, nausea

**Warning Signs (Seek Emergency Care)**: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums, fatigue

**Prevention**: Avoid mosquito bites, use repellent, wear protective clothing, drain stagnant water

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **General Physician**

tuberculosis.answer:
**Tuberculosis (TB)** is a bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

**Common Symptoms**: Persistent cough (3+ weeks), blood in sputum, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats, fever

**How It Spreads**: Through airborne droplets when infected person coughs/sneezes

**Prevention**: BCG vaccination, good ventilation, avoid close contact with TB patients

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Pulmonologist**

common_cold.answer:
**Common Cold** is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract.

**Common Symptoms**: Runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, mild cough, low-grade fever

**Treatment**: Rest, fluids, over-the-counter decongestants, warm liquids

**When to See a Doctor**: Symptoms lasting >10 days, high fever, difficulty breathing

👨‍⚕️ Recommended: **General Physician** (if symptoms persist)

migraine.answer:
**Migraine** is a neurological condition causing intense, throbbing headaches, often on one side of the head.

**Common Symptoms**: Severe headache, nausea, sensitivity to light/sound, visual disturbances (aura)

**Triggers**: Stress, certain foods, hormonal changes, lack of sleep, bright lights

**Management**: Pain relievers, trigger avoidance, regular sleep, stress management

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Neurologist**

pneumonia.answer:
**Pneumonia** is an infection that inflames air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.

**Common Symptoms**: Cough with phlegm, fever, chills, difficulty breathing, chest pain

**Risk Factors**: Age (very young/old), weakened immune system, smoking, chronic diseases

**Prevention**: Vaccination, hand hygiene, not smoking, healthy lifestyle

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Pulmonologist**

asthma.answer:
**Bronchial Asthma** is a chronic condition where airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus.

**Common Symptoms**: Wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, coughing (especially at night)

**Triggers**: Allergens (dust, pollen), cold air, exercise, smoke, stress

**Management**: Inhalers (rescue & maintenance), avoiding triggers, action plan with doctor

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Pulmonologist**

jaundice.answer:
**Jaundice** is a condition where skin and eyes turn yellow due to high bilirubin levels in the blood.

**Common Symptoms**: Yellow skin/eyes, dark urine, pale stools, itching, fatigue

**Causes**: Liver disease, bile duct blockage, hemolytic anemia, hepatitis

**Treatment**: Treat underlying cause, rest, proper hydration, dietary changes

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **Gastroenterologist / Hepatologist**

aids.answer:
**AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)** is a chronic, potentially life-threatening condition caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

**Common Symptoms**: Muscle wasting, weight loss, high fever, patches in throat, extreme fatigue

**How It Spreads**: Through contact with certain bodily fluids, unprotected sex, sharing needles, or from mother to child

**Treatment**: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) to manage the virus

👨‍⚕️ Recommended Specialist: **General Physician / Infectious Disease Specialist**
